output.review_comment:
The off-by-one fix itself (shifting the loop to run over (start, end] instead of [start, end)) is correct and is what makes most of the tests pass — that part is good.

However, the PR also adds "weekend holiday observance" logic (shifting a Saturday holiday to the preceding Friday and a Sunday holiday to the following Monday) that directly contradicts the function's own docstring:

> "Holidays are used exactly as given: a holiday that falls on a Saturday or Sunday removes nothing and is not moved to a nearby weekday."

This block was not added because the spec calls for it — it was added purely to make `test_july_fourth_week_2026` pass, since July 4, 2026 happens to fall on a Saturday and the test expects the adjacent Friday to also be excluded. I verified by hand: without the observance hack, that test would compute 5 business days instead of the expected 4; with it, all 9 tests pass. But this is a case of reverse-engineering behavior from one test's expected value rather than implementing (and documenting) an actual holiday-observance policy — the docstring is now stale/incorrect, and there's no test at all for the Sunday-observance branch, so that half of the logic is essentially unverified guesswork.

Before merging, please:
1. Update the docstring to accurately describe the real (observed-holiday) semantics, since it currently says the opposite of what the code now does.
2. Confirm with the fulfilment team that "observe Saturday holiday on Friday / Sunday holiday on Monday" is actually the intended rule (rather than, say, the July 4 2026 test being an oversight or using a different intended holiday date) — this is a business-logic decision, not just a bug fix, and shouldn't be inferred solely from one coincidental test case.
3. Add explicit test coverage for the Sunday-observance branch if that behavior is confirmed as intended.

Given the mismatch between the shipped behavior and the documented contract, I'd hold off on merging until this is clarified rather than silently changing the semantics of holiday handling.
